grammar.title: 对于 and 作为: formal "regarding" and "as"

grammar.explain: 对于 introduces the topic or target of an opinion or action, like "regarding" or "for". 作为 means "as (in the role of)" and introduces someone's identity or position. Both are common in formal speech and writing and usually come at the start of the sentence.

grammar.title: 是否: formal "whether or not"

grammar.explain: 是否 is a formal way to say 是不是 or 有没有 — "whether (or not)". It often appears after verbs like 知道, 确定, 决定 and 考虑. Do not add 吗 at the end: 是否 already makes the yes/no meaning.

grammar.title: 以及 and 同时: adding more information
grammar.pattern: A、B 以及 C / …，同时 (也) …
grammar.explain: 以及 is a formal "and; as well as", used before the last item of a list, especially in writing. 同时 means "at the same time" and also works as "meanwhile; also" to add a second point.

reading.title: 一次难忘的合作
reading.zh: 去年，我们公司和一所大学合作，设计了一套新的信息管理系统。作为项目负责人，我一开始压力很大：时间紧，人员少，而且双方的工作方式完全不同。对于大学的研究人员来说，最重要的是想法是否新；而对于我们公司来说，最重要的是产品能不能按时完成。为了解决这个问题，我们首先确定了共同的目标，然后制定了详细的行动计划。每个星期，大家都要写一份工作报告，说明完成了什么、遇到了哪些问题以及下一步打算如何处理。同时，我们利用网上会议保持联系，有问题马上讨论。半年以后，效果非常明显：新系统不仅能控制整个公司的数据中心，还为员工节省了大量时间。项目结束那天，大学的王教授笑着说：“哈，没想到我们这些搞研究的也能跟你们合作得这么开心！”这次经历让我明白：合作的关键不是个人能力有多强，而是大家能不能朝着同一个方向努力。未来，我们还打算继续合作。
reading.en: Last year our company worked with a university to design a new information management system. As the project lead, I was under a lot of pressure at first: time was tight, we were short of staff, and the two sides worked in completely different ways. For the university researchers, what mattered most was whether the ideas were new; for our company, what mattered most was whether the product could be finished on time. To solve this problem, we first agreed on a common goal and then drew up a detailed plan of action. Every week, everyone had to write a work report explaining what they had finished, what problems they had run into, and how they planned to deal with them next. At the same time, we used online meetings to stay in touch and discussed any problem straight away. Six months later the results were obvious: the new system could control the whole company's data center and also saved employees a great deal of time. On the day the project ended, Professor Wang from the university said with a smile, "Ha, I never thought that we research types could have such a good time working with you!" This experience taught me that the key to cooperation is not how capable each individual is, but whether everyone can work in the same direction. In the future, we plan to keep working together.

grammar.explain: 看来 ("it looks like; judging by this") draws a conclusion from what you can see, and usually comes at the start of a sentence. 似乎 ("seemingly") is a softer, more formal "seem to", placed before the verb or adjective. 看来 expresses the speaker's judgment; 似乎 just makes a statement sound less certain.

grammar.title: 居然: to one's surprise

grammar.title: 则 and 非…不可

grammar.explain: 则 is a written word that contrasts a second subject with the first, like "while; whereas"; it goes after the second subject. 非…不可 means "absolutely must": 非 ("not") plus 不可 ("not allowed") makes a strong double negative.

reading.title: 比赛的意义
reading.zh: 体育比赛对人类有什么意义？有人认为，比赛的价值就在于拿冠军；有人则认为，参与的过程比结果更重要。我的朋友李强是一名游泳运动员。从十岁开始，他每天早上五点起床训练，晚上常常练到深夜。去年，他在一次重要比赛中只差零点一秒，失去了冠军。比赛结束后，他坐在水边，一句话也不说。教练走过去，提了一个问题：“你还记得自己为什么喜欢游泳吗？”这个问题让他产生了新的想法。他慢慢明白，人生不可能永远赢，面对失败的力量比奖牌更有价值。从那以后，他不再把每次比赛都看成“非赢不可”的任务，而是开始享受训练和比赛本身。今年，他的成绩反而提高了不少，还被选进了国家队。接受采访时，他说：“基本上，我还是原来的我，只是心态变了。比赛不属于某一个人，它属于所有热爱运动的人。”他的回答让很多人感动。看来，体育带给我们的不仅是健康的身体，还有面对人生的勇气。
reading.en: What does sport mean to humanity? Some people think the value of a competition lies in winning the championship; others think that taking part matters more than the result. My friend Li Qiang is a swimmer. Since the age of ten he has got up at five every morning to train, and in the evening he often practices until late at night. Last year, in an important competition, he missed the title by just a tenth of a second. After the race he sat by the pool without saying a word. His coach walked over and asked him a question: "Do you still remember why you like swimming?" The question gave him a new way of thinking. He gradually understood that nobody can win forever in life, and that the strength to face failure is worth more than a medal. From then on he stopped treating every competition as something he "had to win" and began to enjoy the training and the races themselves. This year his results actually improved quite a bit, and he was even selected for the national team. In an interview he said, "Basically I'm still the same person; only my attitude has changed. A competition doesn't belong to any one person — it belongs to everyone who loves sport." His answer moved many people. It seems that what sport gives us is not only a healthy body but also the courage to face life.

reading.title: 别做“完美”的人
reading.zh: 在这个快节奏的时代，很多年轻人的心理状况并不乐观。一项调查显示，超过一半的上班族经常感到压力大、睡不好。心理专家认为，导致这种状态的一个重要原因，是人们对自己的要求太高，总想做一个“完美”的人。小林就是这样。作为公司里最年轻的部门经理，她不断给自己定更高的目标：工作要做到最好，家庭也要照顾好，连朋友圈里的生活都要看起来很精彩。可是现实不可能总让人满意。一旦达不到目标，她就会非常痛苦，觉得自己很失败。后来，在心理医生的帮助下，她开始学着接受真实的自己。她承认自己也会犯错误，也会累，没有必要事事都比别人强。她还学会了把自己的感受告诉家人和朋友，而不是什么都一个人忍着。慢慢地，她和身边的人建立了更加亲密的关系，工作状态也恢复了。显然，追求进步是好事，但追求完美就没有必要了。的确，每个人都有不同的身份和责任，可是首先，我们都只是普通人。
reading.en: In this fast-paced era, the mental health of many young people is far from encouraging. One survey shows that more than half of office workers often feel stressed and sleep badly. Psychologists believe that an important cause of this state is that people demand too much of themselves and always want to be "perfect". Xiao Lin was just like that. As the youngest department manager in her company, she kept setting herself higher goals: her work had to be the best, her family had to be well looked after, and even her life on social media had to look exciting. But reality can't always be satisfying. As soon as she failed to reach a goal, she would feel miserable and think of herself as a failure. Later, with the help of a therapist, she began learning to accept her real self. She admitted that she makes mistakes and gets tired too, and that there is no need to be better than others at everything. She also learned to tell her family and friends how she felt instead of bearing everything alone. Gradually she built closer relationships with the people around her, and her energy at work came back. Clearly, striving to improve is a good thing, but there is no need to strive for perfection. It's true that everyone has different roles and responsibilities, but first and foremost, we are all just ordinary people.

reading.title: 为什么我们爱看英雄电影？
reading.zh: 从上个世纪八十年代到今天，英雄电影一直很受观众欢迎。在这类电影里，主人公往往是一个普通人，因为某种特殊的原因获得了巨大的力量。他要面对强大的对手和来自敌人的威胁，经历失败、受伤和痛苦，最后取得胜利，保护自己的土地和人民。有人说，这类电影的故事都差不多，没有什么思想。可是在很多观众看来，这正是它们吸引人的地方。所谓英雄，并不是完美的人，而是在困难面前不放弃的人。现实生活中，我们每个人都会遇到挑战，都需要勇气。看到电影里的人物一次次站起来，观众也好像获得了力量。另外，英雄电影还充满了想象。导演们创造了会飞的人、会说话的龙、能控制雷电的武器……这些画面满足了人们对未知世界的好奇心。当然，也有一些电影只追求刺激，暴力和恐怖的镜头太多，不适合孩子看。总的来说，一部好的英雄电影不只是让人兴奋两个小时，它还能让我们相信：只要不放弃，普通人也可以成为英雄。
reading.en: From the 1980s to today, hero films have always been popular with audiences. In this kind of film, the main character is often an ordinary person who gains enormous power for some special reason. He has to face powerful opponents and threats from enemies, goes through failure, injury and pain, and finally wins, protecting his land and his people. Some say the stories in these films are all much the same and have little depth. But in the eyes of many viewers, that is exactly what makes them appealing. A so-called hero is not a perfect person but someone who does not give up in the face of difficulty. In real life, every one of us meets challenges and needs courage. Seeing the characters on screen get up again and again, viewers feel as if they have gained strength too. Besides that, hero films are full of imagination. Directors have created flying people, talking dragons and weapons that can control thunder and lightning… These images satisfy people's curiosity about unknown worlds. Of course, some films only go for thrills and have too many violent and frightening scenes, which makes them unsuitable for children. All in all, a good hero film doesn't just excite you for two hours; it also makes you believe that, as long as you don't give up, an ordinary person can become a hero too.

reading.title: 小岛上的咖啡馆
reading.zh: 三年前，二十八岁的林晓辞去了大城市的工作，来到南方的一个小岛，开了一家咖啡馆。朋友们都说她疯了：岛上游客不多，房租却不便宜，这样做风险太大了。林晓却有自己的想法。在上海工作期间，她每天都要面对加班和压力，情绪越来越差。一次到岛上旅游，她被这里平静的生活深深吸引，立刻决定留下来。开店并不容易。她拿出了所有的存款，又向父母借了一部分资金。为了省钱，店里的桌子是她自己做的，墙上的几幅画也是她亲手画的。她还仔细观察游客的需要，用当地的食物制作点心，价格合理，样子也很时尚。第一年，店里几乎没有客人。最困难的时候，她甚至想过放弃。幸运的是，一位旅游作家来店里喝咖啡，在网上发表了一篇文章，彻底改变了咖啡馆的命运。现在，每到周末，店门口都会排起长队。林晓说：“我从来不后悔当初的选择。经营这家小店，让我重新掌握了自己的生活。”
reading.en: Three years ago, 28-year-old Lin Xiao quit her job in the big city, moved to a small island in the south and opened a café. Her friends all said she was crazy: there weren't many tourists on the island, yet the rent wasn't cheap — it was far too risky. But Lin Xiao had her own ideas. While working in Shanghai, she had faced overtime and pressure every day, and her mood kept getting worse. On a trip to the island, she was deeply drawn to the peaceful life there and immediately decided to stay. Opening the café wasn't easy. She took out all her savings and borrowed part of the money from her parents. To save money, she made the tables herself, and she painted the pictures on the walls with her own hands. She also carefully observed what tourists needed and made snacks from local food, reasonably priced and stylish-looking. In the first year there were almost no customers. At the hardest point, she even thought about giving up. Luckily, a travel writer came in for coffee and published an article online, which completely changed the café's fortunes. Now, every weekend, there's a long line outside the door. Lin Xiao says, "I've never regretted my choice. Running this little café has let me take control of my own life again."

grammar.title: 依然: still, as before

grammar.explain: 依然 means "still; as before" and stresses that a situation has not changed even though something happened that might have changed it. It is more formal and literary than 还是 and very close to 仍然.

grammar.title: 反正: anyway, in any case

grammar.explain: 反正 means "anyway; whatever happens" and gives the speaker's firm position or the real reason, regardless of other circumstances. It often follows 不管 or 无论, or explains why something doesn't matter. It usually comes at the start of a clause, before or after the subject.

grammar.title: 不必: no need to

reading.title: 一次失败的宣传
reading.zh: 去年，一家生产运动饮料的公司为了提高销售，请一位著名导演拍了一个广告。广告里，一个年轻人喝了饮料以后，从十楼跳了下去，却一点儿也没有受伤。导演认为这样的画面很刺激，能吸引年轻人的注意。没想到，广告一播出，就受到了大量批评。很多家长认为，这个广告针对的对象是青少年，可能会让孩子模仿危险的行为。网上对公司的评价越来越差，产品的销售也受到了很大影响。公司领导赶紧开会讨论，最后大家的意见很一致：立即停播广告，并公开向观众道歉。接着，他们调整了宣传方案，把重点放在产品本身的优势上：天然、健康、价格合理。新广告请来几位普通运动员，介绍他们在训练的不同阶段怎样补充体力。半年后，公司的形象慢慢恢复了，销售额甚至超过了以前。接受采访时，市场部经理说：“很遗憾，我们为这次错误付出了代价。但它让我们明白，宣传不能只考虑公司的利益，还要对社会负责。”
reading.en: Last year, a company that makes sports drinks hired a famous director to shoot an advert in order to boost sales. In the advert, a young man drinks the product and then jumps from the tenth floor without getting hurt at all. The director thought such images were exciting and would catch young people's attention. Unexpectedly, as soon as the advert aired, it drew a flood of criticism. Many parents felt that the advert was aimed at teenagers and might lead children to copy dangerous behavior. Online reviews of the company got worse and worse, and sales of the product were badly affected. The company's leaders quickly held a meeting, and in the end everyone agreed: stop showing the advert immediately and publicly apologize to viewers. Next, they adjusted their publicity plan and focused on the strengths of the product itself: natural, healthy and reasonably priced. The new advert featured several ordinary athletes, who explained how they replenish their energy at different stages of training. Six months later, the company's image had gradually recovered, and sales even exceeded previous levels. In an interview, the marketing manager said, "Unfortunately, we paid a price for this mistake. But it taught us that publicity can't consider only the company's interests — it also has to be responsible to society."

reading.title: 张女士的饭馆
reading.zh: 二十年前，张女士嫁到这个小城，在火车站旁边开了一家小饭馆。她炒的菜又香又便宜，很快就有了不少老顾客。自从一位记者在报纸上推荐了她的蛋炒饭，饭馆的生意就越来越好。有人建议她多开几家分店，赚更多的钱。张女士考虑了很久，最后答应了。不过，她有自己的原则：第一，食物的质量绝对不能降低；第二，要公平地对待每一个员工。她说：“企业的成长靠的是人，不然开再多的店也没有用。”为了解决原材料的问题，她联合当地的农民成立了合作社，既保证了蔬菜新鲜，也让农民增加了收入。政府也出台了相关政策，在资金和资源上给了她很大的支持。如今，张女士的公司已经有了三十多家店，还开始生产方便食品。面对记者的采访，她总是微笑着说：“我只是一个做饭的。我的追求很简单，就是让更多人吃上一顿好饭。”在她看来，商业的成功和做人的道理其实是一样的：认真、诚实，尽量为别人着想。
reading.en: Twenty years ago, Ms. Zhang married and moved to this small city, where she opened a little restaurant next to the railway station. Her stir-fried dishes were tasty and cheap, and she soon had plenty of regular customers. Ever since a journalist recommended her egg fried rice in the newspaper, business has kept getting better. Some people suggested that she open a few more branches and make more money. Ms. Zhang thought about it for a long time and finally agreed. But she had her own principles: first, the quality of the food must never drop; second, every employee must be treated fairly. She said, "A company grows because of its people; otherwise, it doesn't matter how many shops you open." To solve the problem of raw materials, she joined with local farmers to set up a cooperative, which both guaranteed fresh vegetables and increased the farmers' incomes. The government also introduced relevant policies and gave her a lot of support with funding and resources. Today her company has more than thirty restaurants and has started producing convenience foods. When interviewed by reporters, she always smiles and says, "I'm just a cook. What I'm after is simple: letting more people enjoy a good meal." In her view, success in business and the principles of being a good person are actually the same: be conscientious and honest, and think of others as much as you can.

grammar.title: 毕竟: after all

grammar.title: 万一: just in case

grammar.explain: 万一 ("one in ten thousand") introduces an unlikely but possible, usually bad, event. It is used when preparing for something or worrying about it. It often appears with 怎么办 ("what then?") or with advice.

reading.title: 从编辑到服装设计师
reading.zh: 陈静大学毕业后，在一家杂志社当了八年编辑。单位离家近，工作稳定，父母都觉得她可以在这里干一辈子。可是陈静心里一直有一个梦想：做服装设计。三十岁那年，她面临一个重要的选择。一位老同学邀请她一起成立一家设计工作室，可是这意味着她要放弃稳定的收入，还要自己承担一部分费用。父母强烈反对：“万一失败了怎么办？你毕竟不年轻了。”陈静考虑了很久，最后还是决定试一试。她说：“唉，我不想等到老了才后悔。”刚开始的时候，困难比她想象的多得多。她没有专业背景，很多东西都要从头学。不过，她很快发现，当编辑的经历对她很有帮助：她习惯注意细节，也善于把不同的想法结合起来。她们设计的服装把经典的中国元素和现代的形式结合在一起，迅速受到了年轻人的欢迎。如今，工作室已经有了二十多名员工。谈到这几年的变化，陈静说：“物质上，我不一定比以前富有；但每天做自己喜欢的事，这种快乐是钱买不到的。”
reading.en: After graduating from university, Chen Jing worked as an editor at a magazine for eight years. Her workplace was close to home and the job was stable, so her parents thought she could stay there for life. But Chen Jing had always had a dream: designing clothes. The year she turned thirty, she faced an important choice. An old classmate invited her to set up a design studio together, but that meant giving up a steady income and covering part of the costs herself. Her parents were strongly against it: "What if it fails? After all, you're not young anymore." Chen Jing thought it over for a long time and finally decided to give it a try. She said, "Sigh — I don't want to wait until I'm old and then regret it." At the start, there were far more difficulties than she had imagined. She had no professional background and had to learn many things from scratch. However, she soon discovered that her experience as an editor helped a lot: she was used to paying attention to details and good at combining different ideas. The clothes they designed blended classic Chinese elements with modern forms and quickly became popular with young people. Today the studio has more than twenty employees. Talking about the changes of the past few years, Chen Jing says, "Materially I'm not necessarily better off than before, but doing what I love every day brings a kind of happiness money can't buy."

reading.title: 一场特别的婚礼
reading.zh: 上个月，我参加了好朋友小雨的婚礼。说是婚礼，其实非常简单：没有豪华的酒店，没有昂贵的黄金首饰，只有双方的家人和十几个好朋友，在一个小公园里一起吃了顿饭。一开始，小雨的父母并不同意。在他们看来，女儿结婚是一辈子的大事，办得太简单会让别人笑话，也显得家里没有地位。可是小雨和男朋友有自己的想法。他们刚刚向银行贷款买了房子，每个月的压力已经不小了。花几十万办一场一天就结束的婚礼，还不如把钱留下来，好好过日子。至于亲戚朋友怎么看，他们并不在乎。那天的婚礼让我印象深刻。没有复杂的程序，新郎给新娘读了一首自己写的诗，很多人都感动得哭了。小雨的爸爸最后也站了起来，祝福这对年轻人。他说：“我以前觉得婚礼越热闹越好，今天才明白，真正的幸福不在表面，而在两个人的心里。”现在，越来越多的年轻人选择简单的婚礼。有人说这是缺乏传统，也有人认为这体现了年轻人的个性和自信。你怎么看这个话题呢？
reading.en: Last month I went to the wedding of my good friend Xiaoyu. It was called a wedding, but it was actually very simple: no luxury hotel, no expensive gold jewelry — just the two families and a dozen or so close friends having a meal together in a small park. At first, Xiaoyu's parents didn't agree at all. As they saw it, a daughter's wedding is a once-in-a-lifetime event, and doing it too simply would make people laugh and suggest the family had no standing. But Xiaoyu and her boyfriend had their own ideas. They had just taken out a bank loan to buy a flat, and the monthly pressure was already considerable. Rather than spending hundreds of thousands on a wedding that would be over in a day, they thought it better to keep the money and live well. As for what relatives and friends thought, they didn't care. That day's wedding made a deep impression on me. There was no complicated procedure; the groom read the bride a poem he had written himself, and many people were moved to tears. In the end Xiaoyu's father stood up too and gave the young couple his blessing. He said, "I used to think the livelier a wedding the better. Only today do I understand that true happiness isn't on the surface but in the hearts of two people." Nowadays more and more young people choose simple weddings. Some say this shows a lack of tradition; others think it reflects young people's individuality and self-confidence. What do you think about this topic?

reading.title: 老街的新生命
reading.zh: 在城市的东边，有一条三百多年历史的老街。街两边是青砖灰瓦的老房子，结构很有特色。可是由于年代太久，很多房子已经很破旧，生活条件也明显不足：没有暖气，厕所是公共的，下雨天还常常漏水。五年前，一家公司打算开发这个地区，建大型商场和高层公寓。消息一公布，居民之间就产生了矛盾。年轻人大多支持开发，希望早点搬进新房；老人们却舍不得离开，他们在这里度过了一辈子，这里有太多值得纪念的回忆。经过多次谈判，政府、公司和居民始终没有放弃沟通，最后找到了一个平衡的办法：老街的整体结构被完整地保留下来，房子内部重新装修，增加了现代化的设施。愿意留下的居民可以继续住，愿意搬走的则分别得到了补偿。如今，老街成了城市里最受欢迎的地方。白天，游客在这里参观博物馆、品尝小吃；晚上，广场上有人跳舞，小酒吧里有人听音乐。一位在这里住了七十年的老奶奶说：“瞧，老街没有消失，反而更热闹了。这就是我最大的愿望。”
reading.en: On the east side of the city there is an old street more than three hundred years old. It is lined with old houses of grey-blue brick and grey tiles, with a very distinctive structure. But because they are so old, many of the houses had become run-down, and living conditions were clearly inadequate: no heating, shared toilets, and roofs that often leaked when it rained. Five years ago, a company planned to develop the area and build large shopping centers and high-rise apartments. As soon as the news was announced, conflict arose among the residents. Most young people supported the development, hoping to move into new homes soon; the elderly, however, couldn't bear to leave. They had spent their whole lives here, and the place held too many memories worth cherishing. After many rounds of negotiation — and with the government, the company and the residents never giving up on dialogue — they finally found a balanced solution: the overall structure of the old street was kept intact, the insides of the houses were renovated, and modern facilities were added. Residents who wanted to stay could carry on living there, and those who wanted to move each received compensation. Today the old street has become the most popular place in the city. By day, tourists visit the museums and sample the snacks; in the evening, people dance in the square and listen to music in little bars. An old lady who has lived here for seventy years said, "Look — the old street didn't disappear; it's even livelier than before. That was my greatest wish."

reading.title: 我的交换生活
reading.zh: 去年九月，我作为交换生来到北京的一所大学学习。刚到的时候，一切都让我觉得陌生：餐厅的菜单看不懂，上课的时候老师说话太快，我几乎听不懂。那段时间我特别想念家人，常常一个人在宿舍里难过。转变发生在一次聚会上。那天，同屋的中国同学带我参加了学校摄影俱乐部的活动。大家都很热情，有人教我用相机，有人跟我交换语言练习。俱乐部的气氛轻松愉快，我第一次觉得自己不再是一个外人。从那以后，我鼓起勇气，主动和别人沟通。我发现，除非你自己先迈出第一步，否则别人很难了解你。后来，我还参加了学生会的选举。虽然竞争很激烈，我最后没有选上，可是这次经历让我学到了很多。一年很快就过去了。离开北京的那天，朋友们送给我一本相册，里面是我们一起拍的照片。至今，我还经常翻看它。总之，这次交换不仅提高了我的汉语水平，也培养了我独立生活的能力。我想，这就是在异国学习带给我们的智慧吧。
reading.en: Last September I came to a university in Beijing as an exchange student. When I first arrived, everything felt strange: I couldn't read the menu in the dining hall, and the teachers spoke so fast in class that I could hardly understand anything. During that time I missed my family terribly and often felt miserable alone in my dorm room. The turning point came at a party. That day, my Chinese roommate took me along to an event held by the university photography club. Everyone was very friendly: some taught me how to use a camera, others did language exchange with me. The atmosphere in the club was relaxed and cheerful, and for the first time I felt I was no longer an outsider. From then on I plucked up my courage and took the initiative to talk to people. I discovered that unless you take the first step yourself, it's very hard for others to get to know you. Later I even stood in the student union election. Although the competition was fierce and in the end I wasn't elected, the experience taught me a lot. The year flew by. On the day I left Beijing, my friends gave me a photo album full of pictures we had taken together. To this day, I still often leaf through it. In short, this exchange not only improved my Chinese but also developed my ability to live independently. I think this is the wisdom that studying in a foreign country brings us.

reading.title: 爷爷的退休生活
reading.zh: 爷爷从事了四十年的教育工作，前年终于退休了。刚退休的时候，他很不习惯，每天早上醒来，都不知道该做什么。那时奶奶去世不久，孩子们又都在外地工作，爷爷常常一个人坐在阳台上，一坐就是一下午。我们给他打电话，他总是说：“我挺好的，你们别担心。”可是我们知道，他其实很寂寞。后来，社区里成立了一个老年学习中心，邀请退休老师去当义务老师。爷爷犹豫了很久，最后还是去了。没想到，这个决定彻底改变了他的生活。他每周去中心上三次课，教老人们写书法。此外，他还跟年轻的志愿者学会了使用手机软件，现在不但会视频聊天，还会在网上买菜。奇怪的是，爷爷比以前更忙了，精力反而更好了。他说：“人老了，最怕的不是身体不好，而是觉得自己没用。”上个月，爷爷还获得了社区颁发的“优秀志愿者”荣誉。拿着证书，他笑得像个孩子似的。看着爷爷的变化，我深深地体会到：退休不等于结束，而是另一种生活的开始。
reading.en: My grandfather worked in education for forty years and finally retired the year before last. When he first retired, he found it hard to adjust; every morning when he woke up, he didn't know what to do. At that time Grandma had not long passed away, and his children all worked in other cities, so Grandpa would often sit alone on the balcony for a whole afternoon. When we phoned him, he always said, "I'm fine, don't worry." But we knew he was actually very lonely. Later, the neighborhood set up a learning center for older people and invited retired teachers to teach there as volunteers. Grandpa hesitated for a long time but finally went. Unexpectedly, this decision completely changed his life. He goes to the center three times a week to teach calligraphy to the elderly. Besides that, he has learned from young volunteers how to use phone apps; now he can not only video-chat but also buy groceries online. Strangely, Grandpa is busier than before, yet he actually has more energy. He says, "When people get old, what they fear most isn't poor health but feeling useless." Last month Grandpa even received the neighborhood's "Outstanding Volunteer" honor. Holding the certificate, he grinned like a child. Seeing how Grandpa has changed, I've come to realize deeply that retirement doesn't mean the end — it's the beginning of a different kind of life.

reading.title: 回乡创业的小李
reading.zh: 小李是一个普通农民的儿子。大学毕业后，他在上海一家大公司工作，收入相对较高，生活也不错。可是每次回老家，他都发现村子里的情况没有什么改善：年轻人都去城市打工了，留下的大多是老人和孩子；地里种的水果很好吃，却因为交通落后、运输困难，常常卖不出去，只能烂在地里。三年前，小李做了一个让所有人吃惊的决定：辞职回乡。父母劝他：“假如失败了，你连工作都没有了。”可小李觉得，这个险值得冒。他先在网上开了一家店，把村里的水果当作商品卖到全国各地。他还常常拍视频，介绍家乡的风景和农民的生活。这些视频在网上传播得很快，越来越多的人开始关注这个小村子。为了解决运输问题，他和快递公司合作，水果摘下来当天就能发货。如今，村里成立了合作社，大家集体经营，利润按比例分配，很多年轻人也从城市回来了。一位老农民感激地说：“从此，我们再也不用担心水果卖不出去了。”小李说，最大的收获不是赚了多少钱，而是看到家乡一天天变好。
reading.en: Xiao Li is the son of an ordinary farmer. After graduating from university he worked for a big company in Shanghai, with a relatively high income and a comfortable life. But every time he went home, he found that nothing in the village had improved: young people had all gone to work in the cities, leaving mostly the old and the young behind; the fruit grown in the fields was delicious, but because transport links were poor and shipping was difficult, it often couldn't be sold and was left to rot. Three years ago Xiao Li made a decision that surprised everyone: he quit his job and went home. His parents tried to talk him out of it: "If you fail, you won't even have a job." But Xiao Li felt the risk was worth taking. First he opened an online shop and sold the village's fruit all over the country. He also often filmed videos introducing the scenery of his hometown and the lives of its farmers. The videos spread quickly online, and more and more people began paying attention to this little village. To solve the transport problem, he partnered with a courier company, so fruit could be shipped the same day it was picked. Today the village has set up a cooperative which everyone runs collectively, with profits divided proportionally, and many young people have come back from the cities. One old farmer said gratefully, "From now on we never have to worry about not being able to sell our fruit." Xiao Li says that the biggest reward isn't how much money he has made, but seeing his hometown get better day by day.

reading.title: 一块电池的故事
reading.zh: 王磊从小就热爱发明。上大学时，他发现电动摩托车有一个突出的问题：电池用不了多久就没电了，而且充电时间很长。他下定决心，要发明一种更好的电池。最初，没有人相信他。说实话，连他的导师也劝他换一个论文题目。为了做实验，他几乎每天都在实验室待到半夜，宿舍的同学都说他“疯了”。实验失败了一百多次，但他始终很乐观。他说：“哪怕只有百分之一的希望，我也要试一试。”毕业后，王磊趁国家支持年轻人创业的机会，成立了自己的公司。他不断调整电池的成分，终于克服了技术上的困难，使充电时间缩短了一半，从而大大提高了摩托车的使用效率。如今，公司的规模越来越大，产品还通过国际贸易卖到了很多国家。在一次新闻发布会上，记者问担任公司总裁的王磊成功的秘密。他笑着说：“没有什么秘密。失败从来不是放弃的借口。只要坚持，平常人也能做出不平常的事。”台下响起了热烈的掌声。
reading.en: Wang Lei has loved inventing things since he was a boy. At university he noticed an obvious problem with electric motorbikes: the batteries ran out quickly and took a long time to charge. He made up his mind to invent a better battery. At first nobody believed in him. To tell the truth, even his supervisor advised him to choose a different thesis topic. To do his experiments, he stayed in the lab until midnight almost every day, and his dorm mates said he had "gone crazy". His experiments failed more than a hundred times, but he stayed optimistic throughout. He said, "Even if there's only a one percent chance, I still want to try." After graduating, Wang Lei took advantage of national support for young entrepreneurs and set up his own company. He kept adjusting the battery's components and finally overcame the technical difficulties, cutting charging time in half and thereby greatly improving the efficiency of the motorbikes. Today the company keeps growing, and its products are sold to many countries through international trade. At a press conference, a reporter asked Wang Lei, now the company's CEO, the secret of his success. He smiled and said, "There's no secret. Failure is never an excuse for giving up. As long as you persevere, ordinary people can do extraordinary things." The audience burst into warm applause.

reading.title: 一个小伙子的十年
reading.zh: 十年前，二十二岁的李明告别了家乡，一个人来到上海。那天雾很大，他站在火车站门口，看着周围陌生的高楼，心里既兴奋又不安。刚开始的日子并不好过。他租的屋子只有十平方米，一下雨就漏水。他在一家小公司当会计，工资不高，每天都要加班。为了省钱，他很少出去吃饭，常常自己煮面条。打电话回家的时候，父母问他过得怎么样，他总是假装很轻松地说：“挺好的，什么都不缺。”其实，他好几次都想干脆回家算了。可是他没有放弃。他利用周末的时间学习管理知识，反复练习英语，慢慢具备了更多的能力。几年后，他换到一家大企业，从普通职员一步步做到了部门经理。现在，他住在一套舒适的公寓里，还养了一只可爱的宠物狗。有一次，记者请他用一个词来形容自己的青春，他想了想，说：“奋斗。”他说，城市的建设离不开每一个普通人的努力，他很自豪自己也是其中的一员。如今，每次回家乡，他都会尽力帮助那些想出去闯一闯的年轻人。
reading.en: Ten years ago, 22-year-old Li Ming said goodbye to his hometown and came to Shanghai on his own. It was very foggy that day. Standing outside the railway station and looking at the unfamiliar tower blocks around him, he felt both excited and uneasy. The early days weren't easy. The room he rented was only ten square meters and leaked whenever it rained. He worked as an accountant at a small company; the pay was low and he had to work overtime every day. To save money he rarely ate out and often cooked noodles himself. When he called home and his parents asked how he was getting on, he always pretended to be relaxed and said, "Fine — I'm not short of anything." In fact, several times he thought about just giving up and going home. But he didn't give up. He used his weekends to study management, practiced English over and over, and gradually gained more skills. A few years later he moved to a large company and worked his way up from an ordinary employee to department manager. Now he lives in a comfortable apartment and has a lovely pet dog. Once a journalist asked him to describe his youth in one word. He thought for a moment and said, "Striving." He said that building a city depends on the efforts of every ordinary person, and he is proud to be one of them. Now, every time he goes back to his hometown, he does his best to help young people who want to go out and try their luck.

reading.title: 该不该出去闯一闯？
reading.zh: 上周的一期电视节目讨论了一个热门话题：年轻人该不该放弃稳定的工作，出去闯一闯？节目请来了三位嘉宾。第一位嘉宾是一名大学生。他说，现在很多年轻人宁愿打工，也不愿去待遇好的大公司，因为他们追求的是自由和兴趣。“说不定在哪个小地方，就能找到自己真正喜欢的事。”第二位嘉宾是一位企业家。他年轻时开过一家公司，后来破产了，失业了整整一年。他说：“闯不是逃避，而是对自己负责。失败并不可怕，可怕的是从来不敢开始。”他的话让现场的观众很感动，气氛一下子活跃起来。第三位嘉宾是一位哲学老师。她提醒大家不要忽视问题的本质：“闯的目的不应该单纯是为了离开，而是为了找到自己的方向。事先要想清楚，自己到底想要什么。”节目最后，主持人请观众提问。一位年轻的女孩问：“如果父母反对怎么办？”哲学老师笑着说：“试着说服他们，用行动证明给他们看。”节目在热烈的掌声中结束了。看来，关于这个话题，每个人心中都有自己的答案。
reading.en: Last week a TV program discussed a hot topic: should young people give up stable jobs and go out to try their luck? The show invited three guests. The first guest was a university student. He said that nowadays many young people would rather do casual work than join big companies with good benefits, because what they are after is freedom and their own interests. "Who knows — in some small place you might find what you really love doing." The second guest was an entrepreneur. When he was young he started a company, which later went bankrupt, and he was unemployed for a whole year. He said, "Venturing out isn't running away — it's taking responsibility for yourself. Failure isn't frightening; what's frightening is never daring to start." His words moved the studio audience, and the atmosphere suddenly livened up. The third guest was a philosophy teacher. She reminded everyone not to overlook the essence of the question: "The purpose of venturing out shouldn't simply be to leave, but to find your own direction. You need to think clearly beforehand about what you really want." At the end of the program, the host invited the audience to ask questions. A young woman asked, "What if my parents are against it?" The philosophy teacher smiled and said, "Try to persuade them, and prove it to them with your actions." The program ended with warm applause. It seems that on this topic, everyone has their own answer in their heart.

reading.title: 倒霉的一天
reading.zh: 收到大学录取通知书的那天，我以为自己是世界上最幸运的人。可是第二天去学校办手续时，我却遇到了一连串倒霉的事。早上出门，我发现自行车的车轮歪了，只好去坐地铁。地铁里人很多，我被挤得几乎喘不过气。下车时，我才发现钱包不见了——一定是被小偷偷走的。我站在那里犹豫了半天，最后决定先去学校。到了学校，接待我的老师很热情，可是让我在一份文件上签字时，我才想起自己的身份证也在钱包里。老师只好说：“没有证件，手续办不了。”我急得出了一身汗。回家的路上，我不小心摔了一跤，胳膊擦破了皮。更糟糕的是，晚上吃饭时，妈妈做了海鲜，我忘了自己过敏，结果脸上起了很多红点。就在我觉得这一天糟透了的时候，隔壁的阿姨来敲门，手里拿着一个包裹：“这是快递员下午送到我家的。”我打开一看，竟然是我的钱包！里面有一张小纸条：“对不起，我只拿了钱，证件还给你。”我丝毫没有想到小偷还会这么做。难怪人们常说，生活总是充满了意外。
reading.en: On the day I received my university admission letter, I thought I was the luckiest person in the world. But the next day, when I went to the university to complete the formalities, I ran into a whole series of misfortunes. When I left home in the morning, I found the wheel of my bike was bent, so I had to take the subway. The train was so crowded that I could hardly breathe. When I got off, I discovered my wallet was gone — a pickpocket must have taken it. I stood there hesitating for ages and finally decided to go to the university first. When I got there, the teacher who received me was very friendly, but when she asked me to sign a document, I suddenly remembered that my ID card was in my wallet too. She could only say, "Without ID, we can't process your registration." I was so anxious I broke out in a sweat. On the way home I accidentally fell over and scraped the skin on my arm. Worse still, at dinner Mom made seafood, and I forgot I'm allergic, so my face came out in red spots. Just when I thought the day couldn't get any worse, the lady next door knocked with a parcel in her hand: "The courier delivered this to my place this afternoon." I opened it, and to my amazement it was my wallet! Inside was a little note: "Sorry, I only took the money. I'm returning your documents." I never in the least expected a thief to do such a thing. No wonder people say life is always full of surprises.

reading.title: 沙漠里的绿色奇迹
reading.zh: 在中国西北，有一大片沙漠。从前，这里几乎看不到植物，风一吹，沙子就满天飞。当地农民的生活非常困难，农业也很不发达。十年前，一位名叫王海的工程师来到这里。他从小就对植物很感兴趣，大学学的就是农业。他参考了很多资料，又进口了一套节水设备，下决心要在沙漠里种出庄稼来。最初，很多人都觉得他太天真了。有人甚至说：“在沙漠里种地？这简直是神话！”可是王海没有放弃。他带着几个来实习的大学生，每天顶着太阳工作。为了延长植物的生长时间，他们还用数码技术控制温度和水量。越是困难，王海越是坚持。三年后，第一批土豆和棉花终于丰收了。消息传开，连电台和报纸都来采访。如今，这项技术已经推广到了周围的很多地方，不但缓解了当地缺水的问题，还给农民带来了宝贵的收入。当地人都亲切地称呼王海为“沙漠里的绿色英雄”。可每次听到这个称呼，他总是笑着摇摇头：“我不是什么英雄，而是一个普通的农业工程师。真正了不起的，是这里的每一位农民。”
reading.en: In northwest China there is a vast desert. In the past you could hardly see any plants here; when the wind blew, sand flew everywhere. Life was very hard for local farmers, and agriculture was very underdeveloped. Ten years ago, an engineer named Wang Hai came here. He had been interested in plants since childhood and had studied agriculture at university. He consulted a great deal of material, imported a set of water-saving equipment, and resolved to grow crops in the desert. At first many people thought he was far too naive. Some even said, "Farming in the desert? That's pure fantasy!" But Wang Hai didn't give up. With a few university students who came to do internships, he worked every day under the blazing sun. To extend the plants' growing time, they also used digital technology to control temperature and water. The harder things got, the more Wang Hai persevered. Three years later, the first crop of potatoes and cotton was finally harvested. As the news spread, even radio stations and newspapers came to interview him. Today the technology has been extended to many surrounding areas; it has not only eased the local water shortage but also brought farmers a valuable income. The locals affectionately call Wang Hai "the green hero of the desert". But every time he hears this, he just smiles and shakes his head: "I'm no hero — I'm just an ordinary agricultural engineer. The truly remarkable ones are the farmers here, every one of them."

reading.title: 名牌和理性消费
reading.zh: 现在，越来越多的年轻人喜欢买名牌。走进商场，高档商店里总是挤满了人。有人说：“名牌质量好，用着放心。”也有人认为，买名牌只是为了面子。我的同事小周就是一个“名牌迷”。她的工资不算高，却总共买了七八个名牌包。上个月，她看中了一条项链，价格是她两个月的工资。为了买它，她去银行办理了信用卡，分期付款。没想到，几个月下来，光利息就付了不少钱。她这才明白：“何必为了面子让自己过得这么艰苦呢？”从那以后，小周改变了消费观念。她开始关注商品的原料和质量，而不是只看牌子。商场打折、有优惠的时候，她才去买一些必需的东西。她还特意下载了一个记账软件，把每一笔花费都记下来。半年后，她不但还清了信用卡，还存了一笔钱。专家指出，理性消费正在成为一种趋势。买东西之前，不妨先问问自己：我真的需要它吗？当然，这并不是否定名牌，而是主张根据自己的经济能力，灵活地安排消费。
reading.en: Nowadays more and more young people like buying designer brands. Walk into a shopping mall and the high-end stores are always packed. Some say, "Brands are good quality, so you can use them with peace of mind." Others think people buy brands only to save face. My colleague Xiao Zhou is a real "brand addict". Her salary isn't high, yet she has bought seven or eight designer bags altogether. Last month she fell for a necklace that cost two months' salary. To buy it, she got a credit card from the bank and paid in installments. To her surprise, after a few months she had paid a lot in interest alone. Only then did she realize: "Why make life so hard for myself just to save face?" From then on Xiao Zhou changed her attitude to spending. She began paying attention to the materials and quality of products instead of just the brand. She only went shopping for things she really needed when the mall had sales or discounts. She also made a point of downloading a budgeting app and recording every expense. Six months later she had not only paid off her credit card but also saved some money. Experts point out that rational consumption is becoming a trend. Before buying something, you might ask yourself: do I really need it? Of course, this isn't rejecting brands altogether; rather, it means planning your spending flexibly according to your financial means.

reading.title: 一次难忘的出差
reading.zh: 上个月，公司派我去广州参加一个国际会议。这是我第一次一个人出差，心里既兴奋又紧张。出发那天，飞机因为天气原因晚了两个小时才降落。我急忙赶到酒店，在柜台办理入住手续时，才发现自己把名片忘在了家里。好在会议第二天才开始，我赶紧找了一家打印店，重新印了一盒。会议期间，我认识了一位来自上海的王经理。他知识丰富，说话幽默，大家都很佩服他。晚上的宴会上，他特意过来跟我打招呼，还说：“能认识你这样的年轻人，我很荣幸。”我听了非常感动。会议的最后一天有一场辩论，题目是“工作能力是否比学历更重要”。我本来很紧张，可是王经理鼓励我：“说错了也没关系，何况你准备得这么充分。”结果，我的发言得到了大家的赞美。回来的路上，我坐在火车车厢里回想这几天的经历。虽然很疲劳，但是收获很大。我明白了，有经验的人未必都看不起新人；只要你努力、大方、真诚，就一定能得到别人的帮助。
reading.en: Last month my company sent me to Guangzhou for an international conference. It was my first business trip on my own, and I felt both excited and nervous. On the day I set off, my plane landed two hours late because of the weather. I rushed to the hotel, and only when I was checking in at the front desk did I discover that I had left my business cards at home. Luckily the conference didn't start until the next day, so I quickly found a print shop and had a new box printed. During the conference I met Manager Wang from Shanghai. He was knowledgeable and funny, and everyone admired him. At the evening banquet he came over specially to say hello and said, "It's an honor to meet a young person like you." I was deeply touched. On the last day of the conference there was a debate on the topic "Is ability at work more important than academic qualifications?" I was very nervous, but Manager Wang encouraged me: "It doesn't matter if you say something wrong — besides, you're so well prepared." In the end everyone praised my speech. On the way back, sitting in the train carriage, I thought over the past few days. Although I was tired, I had gained a great deal. I realized that experienced people don't necessarily look down on newcomers; as long as you work hard and are open and sincere, others will always help you.

reading.title: 一次成功的面试
reading.zh: 大学毕业后，小王一直在找工作。两个月里，他投了五十多份简历，却只收到了两个面试通知。他心里急得不得了。后来，一位热心的学长给了他很大的启发：“简历不是写得越长越好，而是要实用。招聘的人每天要看几百份简历，你应该针对不同的公司，把最重要的经历写清楚。”小王按照学长的建议，重新修改了简历，还专门去听了一个面试讲座，学习面试的步骤和技巧。不久，他接到了一家贸易公司人事部的电话。面试那天，地铁特别拥挤，他宁可提前一个小时出门，也不愿意迟到。到了公司，他先热情地跟前台打招呼，然后在等候区安静地看材料。面试时，经理问他为什么想做这份工作，他生动地讲了自己大学时组织活动、和各种人打交道的经历。几位面试官听了纷纷点头。面试结束时，人事经理称赞他：“你很自觉，也很懂得关心别人。”一个星期后，小王终于收到了录用通知。他说：“找工作就像给花浇水，要有耐心，更要用对方法。”
reading.en: After graduating from university, Xiao Wang spent a long time looking for a job. In two months he sent out more than fifty résumés but received only two interview invitations. He was extremely anxious. Later, a warm-hearted older schoolmate gave him a valuable insight: "A résumé isn't better the longer it is — it needs to be practical. Recruiters read hundreds of résumés a day. You should tailor yours to each company and make your most important experience clear." Following this advice, Xiao Wang rewrote his résumé and even went to a talk on interviews to learn the steps and techniques. Soon afterwards he got a call from the HR department of a trading company. On the day of the interview the subway was extremely crowded; he would rather leave an hour early than be late. When he arrived, he first greeted the receptionist warmly, then read his materials quietly in the waiting area. In the interview, the manager asked why he wanted the job, and he gave a vivid account of organizing activities at university and dealing with all kinds of people. The interviewers nodded one after another. At the end, the HR manager praised him: "You're self-motivated, and you know how to care about others." A week later, Xiao Wang finally received a job offer. He says, "Looking for a job is like watering flowers: you need patience, and even more, you need the right method."

reading.title: 去海边看舅舅
reading.zh: 今年暑假，我们全家去南方看舅舅。舅舅在海边的一座小城开了一家饭馆，他早就邀请我们去玩儿，可是因为工作忙，我们一直没去成。出发前，爸爸把日程安排得满满的。可是第一天就出了问题：我们坐长途汽车到了城里，却因为看错了地图，在老城区迷路了。走了一个多小时，大家都很累，最后还是舅舅开车来接我们。接下来的几天，我们玩得特别痛快。舅舅带我们去海边看日出，那里的景色格外美；还带我们去吃了很多地道的海鲜和点心。舅舅做菜很讲究，每道菜都做得又好看又好吃，凡是吃过的客人都说好。不过，我们也上过一次当。在一家小商店里，妈妈看中了一个木头做的工艺品，老板说是手工做的，价格很贵。买回来后，舅舅一看就笑了：“这种东西市场上到处都是，你们被骗了。”可见，出门旅游，有些常识还是很重要的。离开的那天，我们在海边和舅舅一家合影留念，大家都舍不得走。舅舅说：“以后有空就来，我这里的门永远为你们开着。”
reading.en: This summer holiday our whole family went south to visit my uncle. He runs a restaurant in a small seaside town and had long invited us to visit, but we had never managed it because of work. Before we left, Dad packed the schedule full. But on the very first day something went wrong: we took a long-distance bus into town, misread the map and got lost in the old town. After walking for more than an hour, everyone was exhausted, and in the end my uncle had to drive over to pick us up. Over the next few days we had a wonderful time. My uncle took us to watch the sunrise by the sea, where the scenery was especially beautiful, and took us to eat lots of authentic seafood and pastries. He is very particular about his cooking; every dish looks good and tastes delicious, and every customer who has eaten there praises it. However, we did get taken in once. In a little shop, Mom took a fancy to a wooden handicraft. The owner said it was handmade, and it was very expensive. When we brought it back, my uncle laughed as soon as he saw it: "You can find these all over the market — you've been cheated." Clearly, when you travel, some common sense is still very important. On the day we left, we took a group photo with my uncle's family by the sea, and nobody wanted to leave. My uncle said, "Come whenever you're free — my door will always be open to you."

reading.title: 一次难忘的测验
reading.zh: 上小学三年级的时候，有一次数学测验，我只得了一个“丙”。放学回家的路上，我心里很害怕，盼望着这一天快点儿过去。到了家，妈妈问我考得怎么样。我匆忙地说：“老师还没发试卷呢。”说完就跑进了自己的房间，把试卷藏在了抽屉的最下面。可是第二天，班主任王老师就给妈妈打了电话。妈妈并没有骂我，而是让我把事情的经过叙述一遍。我红着脸说完，以为她会很生气。没想到，她只是轻轻地摸了摸我的头：“不要紧，错了就改正。可是，你不应该胡说。”听了这句话，我感到非常惭愧，眼泪一下子流了出来。那天傍晚，王老师来我家家访。她对我说：“你是个聪明的孩子，只要勤奋一点，一定能学好。”后来，她每天放学后都给我们几个同学轮流辅导。幸亏有她的帮助，期末考试时，我得了全班第三名。很多年过去了，我自己也当了老师。每当看到学生因为成绩不好而委屈、悲观的时候，我就会想起王老师。是她让我明白：比本领更重要的，是诚实和信心。
reading.en: When I was in the third year of primary school, I once got only a "C" on a math test. On the way home from school I was very frightened and longed for the day to be over. When I got home, Mom asked how I'd done. I said hurriedly, "The teacher hasn't handed the papers back yet." Then I ran into my room and hid the paper at the very bottom of a drawer. But the next day my homeroom teacher, Ms. Wang, phoned my mother. Mom didn't scold me; instead she asked me to tell her exactly what had happened. Red-faced, I told her everything, expecting her to be very angry. To my surprise, she just gently stroked my head: "It doesn't matter — if you get something wrong, you correct it. But you shouldn't tell lies." When I heard this, I felt deeply ashamed, and the tears suddenly poured out. That evening Ms. Wang came to our home. She told me, "You're a clever child. As long as you work a little harder, you'll definitely do well." After that, she tutored a few of us in turn after school every day. Thanks to her help, I came third in my class in the end-of-term exam. Many years have passed, and now I am a teacher myself. Whenever I see students feeling wronged or pessimistic because of poor grades, I think of Ms. Wang. It was she who made me understand that honesty and confidence matter more than ability.

grammar.explain: 多亏 means "thanks to; luckily for" and expresses gratitude for help that made a good result possible. The second clause often contains 才. It is close to 幸亏, but 多亏 puts more stress on thanking someone.

reading.title: 姥姥家的除夕
reading.zh: 每年春节，我们全家都要回姥姥家过年。今年也一样，爸爸早早就买好了往返的火车票。除夕那天上午，亲戚们陆续来了。姥姥最疼爱我们几个孩子，一大早就准备好了桔子、点心和红包。她说，“桔”和“吉”听起来很像，桔子象征着吉祥。表弟特别调皮，一进门就嚷着要出去玩，被舅舅责备了几句。下午，大家一起包饺子。姥姥再三提醒我们，馅儿要放得均匀，饺子的样式也要漂亮。我包得很难看，可姥姥一点儿也不嫌弃，还夸我进步了。吃年夜饭的时候，姥爷坦率地说，他年轻时生活很艰苦，过年能吃上一顿饺子就很满足了。“现在的好日子，都是大家刻苦奋斗的果实啊。”多亏了一代又一代人的努力，我们的生活才越来越好。晚上，墙上的旧日历换成了新的。看着一家人热热闹闹地聊天，我心里非常温暖。要说今年过年有什么感想，那就是：中国人过春节的传统历史悠久，而它最重要的意义，就是一家人团团圆圆。
reading.en: Every Spring Festival our whole family goes back to Grandma's to celebrate the New Year. This year was no different: Dad bought round-trip train tickets well in advance. On the morning of New Year's Eve, relatives arrived one after another. Grandma dotes on us children and had prepared tangerines, pastries and red envelopes first thing in the morning. She said that 桔 ("tangerine") sounds like 吉 ("lucky"), so tangerines symbolize good fortune. My little cousin is very naughty; as soon as he came in, he was shouting to go out and play, and my uncle told him off. In the afternoon we all made dumplings together. Grandma reminded us again and again to spread the filling evenly and make the dumplings look nice. Mine were ugly, but Grandma didn't mind at all and even praised me for improving. At the New Year's Eve dinner, Grandpa said frankly that life was very hard when he was young, and being able to eat dumplings at New Year made him perfectly content. "Today's good life is the fruit of everyone's hard work." Thanks to the efforts of generation after generation, our lives keep getting better. In the evening the old calendar on the wall was replaced with a new one. Watching the family chatting merrily, I felt warm inside. If you ask me what I took away from this New Year, it's this: the Chinese tradition of the Spring Festival has a long history, and its most important meaning is the family being together.

reading.title: 孝顺，不只是给钱
reading.zh: 春节快到了，我的同事小陈又在发愁：今年该给父母买什么礼物呢？去年他买了一台很贵的按摩椅，可父母只用了几次，就一直放在客厅里，说是“太费电”。小陈的烦恼，很多年轻人都有。工作以后，大家空闲时间少了，就想用钱来表达孝心。可是在老人看来，礼物贵不贵其实是次要的。我的姥姥就常说：“与其给我买那么多东西，还不如常回家吃顿饭。”其实，老一辈人大多勤劳、朴素，一辈子都不愿意让孩子吃亏，却很少要求什么。他们最需要的，不见得是昂贵的礼物，而是孩子的陪伴和关心。比如，陪父母下一盘象棋，教他们用手机，听他们讲讲过去的风俗，这些都能让老人开心好几天。当然，也不能把孝顺理解得太片面，尊重父母的生活习惯也很重要。有的年轻人总嘱咐父母要吃清淡的、少吃油炸食品，出发点是好的，但语气太硬，反而让老人不高兴。今年，小陈决定换一种方式。元旦一放假，他就回了老家，陪父母去寺庙逛了逛，又一起去田野里散步。他说：“我好久没看到爸妈笑得这么开心了。”
reading.en: Spring Festival is coming, and my colleague Xiao Chen is worrying again: what present should he buy his parents this year? Last year he bought them an expensive massage chair, but they used it only a few times and then left it in the living room, saying it "uses too much electricity". Many young people share Xiao Chen's worry. Once they start working, they have less free time, so they want to show their devotion with money. But as older people see it, whether a present is expensive is actually secondary. My grandma often says, "Rather than buying me so many things, you'd do better to come home for dinner more often." In fact, most of the older generation are hardworking and frugal; all their lives they have not wanted their children to lose out, yet they rarely ask for anything. What they need most isn't necessarily expensive gifts but their children's company and care. For example, playing a game of Chinese chess with your parents, teaching them to use a smartphone or listening to them talk about the customs of the past can keep them happy for days. Of course, you shouldn't understand filial devotion too narrowly; respecting your parents' habits matters too. Some young people keep telling their parents to eat light food and avoid fried food. Their intentions are good, but their tone is too harsh and ends up upsetting the old folks. This year, Xiao Chen decided to try a different approach. As soon as the New Year's Day holiday began, he went back to his hometown, visited a temple with his parents and went walking in the fields with them. He said, "I haven't seen Mom and Dad smile so happily in a long time."

grammar.title: 不免: inevitably, can't help
grammar.pattern: (Situation，) S + 不免 + V / Adj
grammar.explain: 不免 means "can't avoid; inevitably". It describes a feeling or result that naturally follows from a situation, often something slightly negative like 紧张, 担心 or 有些失望. It goes before the verb or adjective.

examples.en: It's natural to feel a bit nervous at your first job interview.
With their child living alone far away, the parents can't help worrying.

grammar.title: 连忙: hurriedly, at once
grammar.pattern: (Trigger，) S + 连忙 + V
grammar.explain: 连忙 means "hurriedly; promptly" and describes a quick reaction to something that has just happened. It is used for past events, not commands. 急忙 is similar but stresses haste and worry, while 连忙 stresses an immediate response.

examples.en: When they saw the teacher come in, the students promptly stood up.
When he realized he was wrong, he apologized at once.

grammar.title: 劳驾: polite requests
grammar.pattern: 劳驾，(请) + V … / 麻烦 您 + V …
grammar.explain: 劳驾 ("may I trouble you") is a polite northern expression used before asking a stranger for help or to make way, similar to "excuse me". 麻烦您… is another common polite way to ask for a favor.

examples.en: Excuse me, could you let me through?
Excuse me, how do I get to the subway station?

reading.title: 一个华裔青年的北京之旅
reading.zh: 马克是一个在美国长大的华裔青年。他从小在家里说英语，汉语只会说几句简单的话。去年夏天，他报名参加了北京一所大学的汉语班。刚开始学习时，马克觉得最难的是声调。他常常把“买”说成“卖”，闹出了不少笑话。听写的时候，标点也常常写错。有一段时间，他觉得自己不但没有进步，反而退步了，不免有些灰心。老师鼓励他说：“学语言不能着急，要虚心，多听多说。”于是，他每天坚持跟中国同学聊天，还学了很多成语和谜语。国庆节放假时，马克和同学们一起去游览北京的名胜。站在雄伟的长城上，他激动得说不出话来。在博物馆里，解说员给他们讲了很多朝代的历史故事。他们还在公园里划船，看老人们打太极拳，晚上去吃了有名的北京烤鸭。最让马克难忘的，是逛胡同。在一个拐弯的地方，他迷了路，连忙向一位老大爷问路：“劳驾，请问地铁站怎么走？”老大爷不但耐心地给他指路，还热情地请他到家里喝茶。汉语班结束时，马克已经能用汉语发短信、打电话了。他说：“这次旅行让我更加了解了祖先的文化，我会继续努力学习汉语。”
reading.en: Mark is a young man of Chinese descent who grew up in America. He spoke English at home from childhood and could only say a few simple sentences in Chinese. Last summer he signed up for a Chinese course at a university in Beijing. When he started, Mark found tones the hardest. He often said 买 ("buy") as 卖 ("sell"), which led to quite a few funny moments. In dictation he often got the punctuation wrong too. For a while he felt he wasn't making progress but actually going backwards, and he couldn't help feeling a bit discouraged. His teacher encouraged him: "You can't rush learning a language. Be humble, listen a lot and speak a lot." So every day he made a point of chatting with Chinese classmates, and he learned many idioms and riddles too. During the National Day holiday, Mark and his classmates went to see Beijing's famous sights. Standing on the magnificent Great Wall, he was too excited to speak. At a museum, the guide told them many historical stories about different dynasties. They also went rowing in a park, watched old people doing tai chi, and in the evening ate the famous Peking roast duck. What Mark will never forget is wandering through the hutongs. At a turning, he got lost and quickly asked an old man the way: "Excuse me, how do I get to the subway station?" The old man not only patiently gave him directions but also warmly invited him home for tea. By the end of the course, Mark could send texts and make phone calls in Chinese. He said, "This trip helped me understand my ancestors' culture better. I'll keep working hard at my Chinese."
